ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, triangle ABC is a 5-12-13 right triangle, C is at the lower left, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower right; M is on AC, N is on BC, J and K are on AB, and MJ, NK are perpendicular to AB. According to the coordinate method, let C=(0,0), A=(0,5), B=(12,0). Because CM=4 and M is on AC, M=(0,4); because CN=4 and N is on BC, N=(4,0). Line AB passes through (0,5) and (12,0), and its equation is 5x+12y-60=0. MJ and NK are perpendicular to AB, so their lengths are respectively the distances from M, N to line AB. MJ=|5(0)+12(4)-60|/sqrt(5^2+12^2)=12/13. NK=|5(4)+12(0)-60|/13=40/13. Next, JK is on AB, and MJ and NK are two mutually parallel perpendicular lines, so the height of trapezoid MJKN is equal to the distance between the two perpendicular lines along the AB direction. Vector MN=(4,-4), and the unit vector in the AB direction can be taken as (12,-5)/13, therefore the projection length is MN·(12,-5)/13=(48+20)/13=68/13. So the area of trapezoid MJKN is (1/2)(12/13+40/13)(68/13)=136/13. Triangle CMN is a right triangle, and its area is (1/2)(4)(4)=8=104/13. Therefore the area of pentagon CMJKN is 136/13+104/13=240/13.

method.method_draft: Compute the area by subtracting two small right triangles from triangle ABC. Since AB=13, AC=5, BC=12, triangle ABC is right at C and has area 30. The pentagon CMJKN is the whole triangle ABC minus triangle AMJ near A and triangle BKN near B. Because MJ and NK are perpendicular to AB, triangles AMJ and BKN are right triangles, and each is similar to the original 5-12-13 triangle ABC: triangle AMJ shares angle A, and triangle BKN shares angle B. Since CM=4 on AC=5, AM=1, so the scale factor for triangle AMJ relative to ABC is AM/AB=1/13, giving area 30/169. Since CN=4 on BC=12, BN=8, so the scale factor for triangle BKN relative to ABC is BN/AB=8/13, giving area 30*(8/13)^2=1920/169. Therefore the pentagon area is 30-30/169-1920/169=3120/169=240/13.
